Draft 1 of 4 · bugs/rr-threshold-phantom-count.md

Zoho comparison verdict: BUG

Zoho counts exactly the agent's real Open tickets in the rule's department; TAVI counts 1–2 tickets that do not exist, so tickets wait while the agent is under the limit. (Zoho: Setup text + live test 9 Nov.)

Round Robin Assignment | Department threshold counts Open tickets the agent does not have, so tickets wait while the agent is under the limit


Summary For some agents, the round robin department threshold counts one or two more Open tickets than the agent really has in that department. New tickets then stay unassigned (backlog) although the agent is under the threshold. The extra tickets appear in no ticket list and not in the agent's workload. Found while retesting NDC-2824 and NDC-2970 (both pass on the threshold logic itself).
Steps to Reproduce
  • Open Desk > Tickets, filter QA AO Dept B by owner Test User 1 and status Open: 4 tickets (#4281, #4282, #4283, #4285). The agent's workload shows the same 4.
  • Go to Setup > Assignment Rules > Round Robin, QA AO Dept B. Create a rule whose only agent is Test User 1 (Sequential), matching a test subject.
  • In the department's round robin settings, turn on "Department threshold", set it to 5, allow offline agents, and save.
  • Create a ticket in QA AO Dept B that matches the rule. It stays unassigned.
  • Set the threshold to 6 and create another matching ticket. It stays unassigned.
  • Set the threshold to 7 and create another matching ticket. It is assigned to Test User 1.
  • Repeat steps 2–6 for Dev Team 2 (1 Open ticket, #4284): threshold 2 waits (tried 3 times), threshold 3 assigns.

    • Expected Result
  • The threshold counts only the agent's real Open (and Escalated) tickets in that department, the same tickets the list and the workload show.
  • With 4 Open tickets, a threshold of 5 lets the next ticket go to Test User 1; with 1 Open ticket, a threshold of 2 lets the next ticket go to Dev Team 2.

    • Actual Result
  • Test User 1: real Open 4, rule counts 6 (+2). #4588 (thr 5) and #4589 (thr 6) wait; #4590 (thr 7) is assigned. Same at 12:01Z (#4584/#4585) and in every run earlier in the day.
  • Dev Team 2: real Open 1, rule counts 2 (+1). #4586, #4606, #4610 (thr 2) wait; #4587, #4608, #4611 (thr 3) are assigned. This extra count started around 11:25Z on 16 Nov.
  • Control: Test User 1 in QA AS6 Dept A (74 Open) is assigned at threshold 75, so the count is right in that department.
  • Ruled out in clean probes (none raised the count): On Hold tickets, tickets moved to another department, tickets reassigned away, tickets closed, an auto-assigned ticket deleted later, a ticket deleted right after create.

    • Environment staging-desk.taviportal.com (NDC-Staging), owner account, API + Setup, 16 Nov 2026, 12:00–12:14Z.
    Suggested priority: Medium (agents get fewer tickets than their limit; tickets go to backlog with no visible reason)
    Related: NDC-2824, NDC-2970, NDC-2275 (the first NF-3 burst at dept threshold 5 was skewed by this); possibly linked to the ticket-without-number defect (ticket-no-number-no-history.md), which appeared at the same time as Dev Team 2's extra count.
    Evidence: BUG-rr-threshold-phantom-count-FAIL.png

    Draft 2 of 4 · bugs/ticket-no-number-no-history.md

    Zoho comparison verdict: BUG

    Zoho numbered all 5 parallel creates at once (#114–#118, consecutive) with History on the first read; TAVI left a ticket without number/History for 34 min and 5 of 10 burst tickets for up to 47 s.

    Tickets | A created ticket can stay without a ticket number and History until someone opens it


    Summary A ticket created through the Records API was saved, but for 34 minutes it had no ticket number and an empty History and activity feed, even after it was edited to Closed. The Desk part of the ticket (number, History) was only created when the ticket was first opened, and it then got the next free number (#4583) instead of a number from the time it was created. A parallel burst of 10 creates showed the same step running late (up to 47 seconds), but in that burst every ticket got its number in the end.
    Steps to Reproduce
  • In QA AO Dept B, with a one-agent round robin rule active and a department threshold set, create a ticket through the Records API (the NDC-2824 retest probe "QA RT19 AS R19AS4seunc b1thr3", 16 Nov 11:25:19Z).
  • About 20 seconds later, edit the ticket to Closed.
  • Look at the ticket in the Records API / tickets data: it has no ticket number. Open its History: empty.
  • Open the ticket page.
  • For the burst: create 10 tickets at once in the same department and check their numbers and History 20 seconds later.

    • Expected Result
  • Every ticket gets its ticket number and a "Ticket created" History entry as soon as it is created, and later edits (status Closed) are recorded.
  • No ticket stays without a number; numbers follow creation order.

    • Actual Result
  • Record 4e6a4894 (created 11:25:19Z): at 11:59Z it was the only one of 790 tickets with no ticket_number. History and activity were both empty, although the status was changed to Closed at 11:25:42Z.
  • The first open of the ticket (GET of the ticket at 11:59:54Z) created the Desk ticket at that moment (created_at 11:59:54Z) with number 4583, out of order: the next ticket created at 11:25 got #4545.
  • Number 4546 is used by no live ticket and no Recycle Bin item. A ticket created and deleted at once at 11:26Z is in the Recycle Bin with no number at all.
  • Parallel burst of 10 (12:07:10Z): all 201; after 20 s, 5 of the 10 had no number and no activity. Their Desk side was created one by one, 2–47 s after create; all had numbers by 12:08. No lasting ghost from the burst.
  • Two more tries did not leave a ghost: create then close at once (x2), create then edit priority at once — all numbered within 10 s.
  • How the first ghost was made: a single API create (not a burst) while other test lanes were creating tickets at the same time; the exact trigger is not known.

    • Environment staging-desk.taviportal.com (NDC-Staging), owner account, Records API, 16 Nov 2026, 11:25–12:10Z.
    Suggested priority: Medium (a ticket can stay without number and History, and outside assignment/SLA processing, until someone opens it)
    Related: NDC-2275 (NF-3 burst test), NDC-2824; round robin phantom count (rr-threshold-phantom-count.md) started at the same time for Dev Team 2.
    Evidence: BUG-ticket-no-number-no-history-FAIL.png (no UI screenshot: the ghost was fixed by its first open, and the burst tickets were numbered within 47 s)

    Draft 3 of 4 · bugs/import-owner-name-not-matched.md

    Zoho comparison verdict: NOT A BUG

    Zoho matches Ticket Owner only by Agent ID / External Id / Email (no name option) — as you said, email is the key. Unmatched rows: Zoho creates them Unassigned and reports Failed 0 with no warning; TAVI gives them to the importer (your GEN-13 decision, 9 Nov) and reports 0 errors. Same silence. A warning would be a nice extra, not a parity bug.

    Ticket Import | Ticket Owner given by agent name is not matched and silently replaced by the importer, result shows 0 errors


    Summary When tickets are imported with a Ticket Owner column that holds the agent's name, the owner is never matched, even for an active agent who is a member of the ticket's department. Every such ticket is given to the person who runs the import. The import finishes as "Import complete" with 0 errors, so the user is not told that the owners were replaced. The same owner given as the agent's email address is matched correctly. Seen first in the NDC-2275 retest (#4558).
    Steps to Reproduce
  • Prepare a CSV with columns Subject, Department, Status, Priority, Ticket Owner and two rows in QA AS6 Dept A: one with Ticket Owner "Test User 1" (member of QA AS6 Dept A), one with "Mahmoud Samy" (an agent who is not a member of that department).
  • Go to Setup > Data > Import, choose Tickets, upload the file, Add new records.
  • On Map fields, check that Ticket Owner is mapped to Ticket Owner.
  • On Assign, leave "Trigger automation and process management" unticked. Submit.
  • Look at the Result page and open the two new tickets.
  • Repeat with automation ticked.
  • Repeat with one row whose Ticket Owner is Test User 1's email address.

    • Expected Result
  • A row whose owner names an eligible agent (here Test User 1) gets that agent as owner, whether the file gives the name or the email.
  • A row whose owner cannot be used (not found, or not in the department) is shown on the Result page as an error or warning (e.g. "Row 3: owner 'Mahmoud Samy' is not in QA AS6 Dept A; assigned to you"), and the error count includes it.

    • Actual Result
  • Automation unticked: #4622 (Test User 1) and #4623 (Mahmoud Samy) are both owned by the importer.
  • Automation ticked: #4624 and #4625, same.
  • Each import session stores, for both rows, "No eligible user matches '<name>'.", but error_count is 0. The Result page says "Import complete", 0 Errors, and the history row says "2 added · 0 errors".
  • With the email address, #4630 is owned by Test User 1 (matched, no errors).
  • The earlier NDC-2275 import (#4558, owner "Mahmoud Samy") behaved the same way.

    • Environment staging-desk.taviportal.com (NDC-Staging), owner account, Setup > Data > Import (Tickets), QA AS6 Dept A, 16 Nov 2026 12:27–12:40Z.
    Suggested priority: Medium (imported tickets silently go to the wrong owner; nothing on screen tells the user)
    Related: NDC-2275
    Evidence: BUG-import-owner-name-not-matched-FAIL.png

    Draft 4 of 4 · bugs/skills-api-silent-drop.md

    Zoho comparison verdict: NOT A BUG

    Zoho also returns 200 and silently drops inactive and other-department skills (create and edit; editing with only such a skill empties the list). TAVI refusing deleted/unknown skills with 422 is stricter than Zoho — a TAVI extra.

    Ticket Skills | Inactive and other-department skills are silently dropped on save while a deleted skill is refused


    Summary When a ticket is created or edited with a list of skills, a deleted or unknown skill is refused with 422 "not one of the allowed values", but inactive skills and skills of another department are accepted with 200/201 and silently removed. The caller is not told which skills were dropped, and an edit that sends only another department's skill removes all skills from the ticket. Found while retesting NDC-2933 and NDC-2971; re-run fresh at 12:27Z.
    Steps to Reproduce
  • In QA AS6 Dept A (skills S1, S2 active, "QA RT19 AS Inact" inactive), create a ticket through the Records API with skills [S1, QA RT19 AS Inact].
  • Create a ticket with skills [S1, QA SK13 S1] (a skill of another department).
  • Edit a ticket with skills [S2, QA RT19 AS Inact], then [S2, QA SK13 S2].
  • Edit a ticket with only [QA SK13 S2].
  • For comparison, create or edit a ticket with [S1, QA RT19 AS Del] (a deleted skill) or with a skill name that does not exist.

    • Expected Result
  • One rule for every skill that is not allowed: either refuse the request with 422 naming each such skill (as for a deleted skill), or save and return a warning listing the skills that were dropped.

    • Actual Result
  • Deleted skill and unknown skill: 422 RECORD_VALIDATION_FAILED, "Skills: '<name>' is not one of the allowed values." on create and on edit; nothing saved (correct).
  • Inactive skill on create: 201, #4618 saved with S1 only, no warning.
  • Other-department skill on create: 201, #4619 saved with S1 only, no warning.
  • Inactive / other-department skill on edit: 200, #4620 saved with S2 only, no warning.
  • Edit with only another department's skill (NDC-2933 run, 11:4xZ): 200, the ticket's skills become empty, no warning.

    • Environment staging-desk.taviportal.com (NDC-Staging), owner account, Records API, 16 Nov 2026 12:27Z.
    Suggested priority: Low
    Related: NDC-2933 (the ticket page Edit Skills list still offers these skills and drops them without telling the user — tracked there), NDC-2971
    Evidence: BUG-skills-api-silent-drop-FAIL.png
